question: National Youth Day is celebrated on the birth date of which of the following personalities?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Youth Day is celebrated annually on **January 12** in India.
 
• This day marks the birth anniversary of **Swami Vivekananda**, a revered Indian monk and philosopher.
 
• The Government of India declared Swami Vivekananda's birthday as National Youth Day in **1984**.
 
• Swami Vivekananda is known for his teachings on youth empowerment and his speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in **1893**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda's Contributions**

 
 
• Swami Vivekananda was a disciple of **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa** and played a key role in introducing Indian philosophies to the Western world.
 
• He founded the **Ramakrishna Mission** in 1897, which focuses on social service and education.
 
• His teachings emphasize the importance of youth in nation-building and self-improvement.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Date**
 
 
• January 12 is chosen to inspire the youth of India to follow Swami Vivekananda's ideals and principles.
 
• The day includes various activities and events such as seminars, youth conventions, and essay-writing competitions.
 
 
 
• **Parliament of the World's Religions**
 
 
• Held in Chicago in 1893, where Swami Vivekananda delivered his famous speech starting with "Sisters and Brothers of America."
 
• This speech is considered a significant moment in introducing Hinduism and Indian spirituality to the Western world.
 
 
 
• **Legacy and Influence**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda's teachings continue to influence Indian youth and are integrated into various educational curricula.
 
• He is often credited with awakening India’s sense of nationalism and advocating for a spiritual and cultural resurgence.
